overview: A single-page restricted State Department telegram of January 8, 1946 authorizing the U.S. Legation in Stockholm to act regarding Okumura and other Japanese journalists, while leaving the handling of Mrs. Kitamura to the Legation’s discretion. The message responds to Stockholm telegram no. 19 of January 3 and was filed under press, news-gathering agencies, nationality, and field of operation.

subfiles.title: Telegram authorizing action concerning Okumura and Japanese journalists
subfiles.about: The Department authorizes the Legation to act regarding Okumura and Japanese journalists and leaves Mrs. Kitamura’s case to its discretion.
subfiles.summary: In response to the Legation’s telegram no. 19 of January 3, the State Department grants the requested authorization concerning Okumura and Japanese journalists. It instructs the Legation to exercise its own discretion regarding Mrs. Kitamura. The telegram is classified restricted and bears the file reference 894.91200/12-1445.

interest: This brief telegram offers evidence of U.S. diplomatic oversight of Japanese journalists operating internationally immediately after the Second World War. Its distinction between general authorization for Okumura and other journalists and discretionary treatment of Mrs. Kitamura may be useful for studying occupation-era mobility, press controls, gendered administrative treatment, and the overseas activity of Japanese news personnel.
